title: INCONVENIENT: A Benchmark to Assess LLM Generalization Capabilities from Convenience Samples
abstract: arXiv:2610.21038v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Machine learning models for tabular prediction typically assume that training data are representative of the population on which they will be deployed. In practice, however, data are often collected based on convenience, availability, or cost, resulting in systematic sampling biases that can distort feature--target relationships and undermine real-world generalization. Existing tabular distribution-shift benchmarks primarily construct out-of-distribution (OOD) settings by partitioning observations across naturally occurring domains. While such partitions may induce changes in P(Y | X), the resulting shifts are neither explicitly controlled nor isolated, and the evaluation distributions themselves are often not representative of the broader target population. translated_title: INCONVENIENT：一个评估大语言模型从便利样本中进行泛化能力的基准
translated_abstract: 用于表格预测的机器学习模型通常假设训练数据能够代表其将要部署的目标人群。然而在实践中，数据往往出于便利性、可获得性或成本的考虑而收集，由此产生的系统性抽样偏差可能扭曲特征与目标变量之间的关系，并损害模型在真实世界中的泛化能力。现有的表格数据分布偏移基准主要通过在自然存在的域之间划分观测样本来构建分布外（OOD）设置。虽然这种划分可能引起 P(Y | X) 的变化，但由此产生的偏移既未被显式控制也未被隔离，而且评估分布本身往往无法代表更广泛的目标人群。我们提出了 INCONVENIENT，一个旨在研究模型对便利样本偏差鲁棒性的基准。INCONVENIENT 不依赖自然存在的域划分，而是直接……
tldr: 提出了INCONVENIENT基准，通过显式构造并隔离便利样本偏差，评估模型在有偏采样的表格数据上向目标总体泛化的能力。
en_tdlr: We introduce INCONVENIENT, a benchmark that explicitly controls and isolates convenience-sample bias to assess models' ability to generalize from biased tabular samples to the broader target population.
